round1_to_round2.what_moved: Every agent took the round-1 supervisor facts on board (fee ~$0.49/share, core 2026 FCF ~$11B, net debt ~$5.2B, 4,164M basic shares, FY27 consensus $3.83-3.85, Q3 consensus $0.82, PSKY-WBD cleared). The verified H1'26 content-spend finding (+32%, cash/amortization ~1.16x) moved four agents down: agents 1, 2 and 4 to $77 and agent 5 to $74. Agent 3 moved up from $69 to $71 because its core FCF base was raised to $11B. The mean fair value fell from $77.2 to $75.2, mean P(>=67) from 0.555 to 0.541, and mean P(>=67.06) for one month from 0.510 to 0.504. Thesis breaks did not move.
round1_to_round2.independence_verdict: Mostly anchoring rather than independent agreement. (1) The fair-value spread almost halved (SD $4.4 to $2.4; P(>=67) range 0.06 to 0.025), and three agents now land on exactly $77 using nearly the same recipe: an FY27/FY28 NTM blend of ~$4.25-4.30, 18.5x, a 4.5% FCF yield and ~$13.5B of 2028 FCF. In round 1 they used 16-20x and yields of 4.0-5.0%. (2) Source overlap doubled (mean Jaccard 0.061 to 0.108; distinct share 0.84 to 0.75). Most new citations are the same filings and press pages the supervisor cited, and agent 4 cites the supervisor's file itself. (3) Agent 4's ladder cut (P(>=67) 0.59 to 0.546) answers the supervisor's request directly; it brought no new datum. (4) Agents 2 and 5 now have identical 1-month ladders, because both use a lognormal centred at $67.2 with 12% sigma. That is the same recipe, not two confirmations. Adopting verified facts is legitimate convergence. The narrowing on multiple and yield is not, because no new evidence settled them. Signs of independence remain: every agent kept its own thesis break and said why it disagreed with the supervisor's $49; agent 3 still disputes the supervisor's 18x/4.25%; agent 5 brought a new (thin) base rate that argues for a flat multiple; agent 2 re-weighted to Netflix-specific Antenna churn. Treat the round-2 consensus as roughly two or three independent views, not five, and do not narrow the distribution because the agents agree.

disagreements.topic: How much the content-spend finding should cut FCF and fair value
disagreements.positions: In round 2 agents 1, 2, 4 and 5 cut 2027-28 FCF growth to ~11-12%/yr (2028 FCF ~$13.5-13.9B) and fair values by $2-4. Agent 3, the skeptic, already had this in round 1 and moved up. All cite H1 OCF ex-fee down ~19%.
disagreements.resolution: The content-spend fact is right (H1 additions $9.77B vs $7.39B; payments 1.16x amortization). But the Q2'26 10-Q also discloses $729M of non-routine H1 payments for prior-period Brazil non-income tax assessments in working capital, which no agent mentioned. Excluding both the fee-related tax and this item, recurring OCF fell ~5% in H1, not ~19%. The Brazil cash outflow does not recur in 2027, which adds ~$0.7B to 2027 FCF growth off the ~$11B 2026 base. The FCF cuts are therefore a little too deep, by ~$0.5B of 2028 FCF or ~$1-2/share in the FCF methods and ~$0.5-1 in blended fair value. Q3 cash flow (2026-10-20) will show whether content payments normalise.
disagreements.evidence: Q2'26 10-Q cash flow statement and MD&A (OCF $7,034M; additions to content assets $9,774M; change in content liabilities -$137M; amortization $8,529M; '$729 million of non-routine payments made in connection with non-income tax assessments in Brazil for prior tax periods'; Q2 OCF -$679M YoY driven by +$1,059M content payments and -$620M working capital).

thesis_break_reason: $49 is ~12.8x checked FY2027 consensus (~$3.84) and ~15.8x core 2026 EPS (~$3.10), below Netflix's 2022 trough multiple and Wells Fargo's $57 bear target. Reaching it within a year would take a broken earnings base: a January 2027 guide with single-digit revenue growth or margins below 2026's 31.5%, an FCF guide cut because content payments keep running above ~1.15x amortization, falling UCAN memberships, or a large levered acquisition. FCF conversion: H1'26 content payments were 1.16x amortization (additions +32%), and ~$5.9B of H2 FCF is needed for the ~$12.5B guide (~$11B core). H1 OCF also carried a non-recurring $729M Brazil tax payment, so the recurring deterioration is smaller than the headline -19%.
Valuation: ~17.5x FY2027 consensus and ~3.9% on core FCF, with net debt of ~$5.2B and $27.1B of buyback authorization retiring ~3-4% of shares a year.

Engagement and share loss to YouTube (Nielsen July: 7.8% vs 14.2%) drove the Wells Fargo Underweight ($57) and HSBC Hold ($76, 2026-09-22) calls. Netflix-specific churn holds at ~2% (Antenna), and ads expand to 15 more countries in 2027 (9 EMEA on 2027-03-01).

fair_value.reason: ~18x NTM EPS at Oct-2027 of ~$4.25 (FY27 ~$3.80 / FY28 ~$4.40-4.50) = ~$76.5. Equity-level FCF method: NTM FCF at Oct-2027 ~$13.6B (core 2026 ~$11B, plus ~$0.7B of non-recurring Brazil tax cash that does not repeat, grown ~11%/yr with content payments ~1.12-1.15x amortization) over ~4.03B diluted shares = ~$3.37 at a 4.4% yield on market cap = ~$76.6, with no separate net-debt deduction because the yield benchmark is market-cap based. Weighted 60/40 that gives ~$76. summary: Round 2 is mostly anchoring on the round-1 supervisor file. Every agent adopted the verified facts, which is correct, but fair values compressed from $69-81 to $71-77 (three at exactly $77) on near-identical multiples and yields that no new evidence settled. The agents' new facts check out against filings and primary announcements. They all missed that H1'26 OCF carried a non-recurring $729M Brazil tax payment, so recurring cash deterioration is smaller than the -19% headline. With that and a net-debt double count fixed, fair value is ~$76 (mean $75.2), the thesis break stays at $49, and both ladders stay at the round-2 mean (P(>=67) 0.54 at 12 months, 0.50 at one month), with confidence low. The Q3 print on 2026-10-20 (content-payment normalisation, FCF guide) and the January 2027 margin guide decide the multiple. I put the chance that NFLX beats SPY on 12-month Sharpe at ~0.44, with a 4% cap and no entry before the print.
brief_feedback: The round-2 revise brief shows agents the supervisor's fair value and multiples, which caused visible anchoring (three agents at $77 with 18.5x/4.5%). Pass only the verified facts and corrections to agents, not the supervisor's fair value, multiple or ladder.
